QF.id: AIFM CIII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_50

question.text: Mr. Arjun Reddy, ops head at Nilgiri Multi-Strategy Fund (close-ended 6-year Cat III), is preparing for the tenure-end. Liquid positions are 82% of NAV; 18% remains illiquid at month -3. The optimal playbook is to:

answer.text: Sell illiquid positions at any price before tenure end
Enter the 1-year Liquidation Period; attempt 25%-bid arrangement; if unresolved, seek 75% consent for Dissolution Period filing via merchant banker
Extend tenure unilaterally by 2 years without investor consent
Transfer illiquid positions to the IM's proprietary book

explanation.text: The Logic: The correct regulatory sequence is: on tenure expiry, enter the 1-year Liquidation Period; during that window, arrange bids for at least 25% of the value of unliquidated investments and pursue in-specie distribution with 75% investor consent; if assets remain unliquidated, file the merchant-banker Information Memorandum + Due-Diligence Certificate before Liquidation Period expiry to enter the Dissolution Period (also subject to 75% investor consent). The Dissolution Period cannot exceed the original scheme tenure. The Trap: Fire-sale (A) destroys value and creates mis-selling risk. Unilateral extension (C) is not permitted — tenure extension needs two-thirds-by-value consent. Transfer to the IM's book (D) is a related-party transaction that breaches fiduciary duty. Note: The Liquidation Period (p. 357), 25% bid floor (pp. 357-358), 75% consent for in-specie / Dissolution Period (p. 358), pre-expiry merchant-banker filing (p. 359) and two-thirds-by-value tenure extension (p. 398) together define this end-of-life pathway.
